title: [GDScript] Reduce changes in refcounts in GDScript VM
body:
Original PR: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/118507

## Technical overview
Uses const references for `StringName` to not copy them by value, because copying them by value increases their ref count on creation and destruction.

Seeing what op codes are affected in this PR, it is unlikely this affects performance too much on master, but this can lead to random lag spikes when using multi-threading if Godot construct 2 or more of the same `StringName` at the same time from different threads. And seeing that you want to parallelize your work when using threads, it means you will usually call the same static function or the same instance function from different instances, which will run the same code in a loop from different threads. And because of this the chances of that happening are not small... well they are also not large.

Currently because of value returns from array and dictionary this won't actually prevent lag spikes related to them, but it will lessen them.

## VM Improvements
Debug and Release:
- `OPCODE_TYPE_TEST_ARRAY`
- `OPCODE_TYPE_TEST_DICTIONARY`
- `OPCODE_TYPE_TEST_NATIVE`
- `OPCODE_ASSIGN_TYPED_ARRAY`
- `OPCODE_ASSIGN_TYPED_DICTIONARY`
- `OPCODE_CONSTRUCT_TYPED_ARRAY`
- `OPCODE_CONSTRUCT_TYPED_DICTIONARY`
- `OPCODE_RETURN_TYPED_ARRAY`
- `OPCODE_RETURN_TYPED_DICTIONARY`
- `OPCODE_CALL_UTILITY`

In the process of testing I also found that typed containers return value copies, which will increase their ref count, so multi-threaded operations for typed containers will not receive as much benefits as `OPCODE_CALL_UTILITY` and `OPCODE_TYPE_TEST_NATIVE`. The methods in question:
- `array->get_typed_class_name()`
- `array->get_typed_script()`
- `dictionary->get_typed_key_class_name()`
- `dictionary->get_typed_key_script()`
- `dictionary->get_typed_value_class_name()`
- `dictionary->get_typed_value_script()`

`OPCODE_CALL_UTILITY` was hard for me to call, as I often called `OPCODE_CALL_UTILITY_VALIDATED` by mistake, but it is possible and it gets slower in multi-threading on master.

I didn't change it in `OPCODE_CALL`, because const reference to ternary doesn't improve performance. Well and it will also conflict with the PR that aims to optimize debug calls.

## Performace testing
Build commands are the same as in the original PR.
Test project: [testthreads4.6_target.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26926113/testthreads4.6_target.zip)

The basic test was to divide the iterations between threads and to perform the most basic interaction inside the loop, in theory this should imitate doing parallelizable work. The number of iterations was 200_000_000.

The results are presented as tables. In the columns was written the number of threads this attempt used, 0th thread is main thread that serves as the control.
Column type:
- `debug` - tested it in launched from Godot project
- `tool` - tested it inside tool script in editor
- `release` - tested it in export release

Tested on:
- EndeavourOS on X11 
- X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors 
- Vulkan (Forward+) 
- dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650 (nvidia; 595.58.03) 
- Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-9300H CPU @ 2.40GHz (8 threads) 
- 15.49 GiB memory

<details>
<summary>func_base, this one is fine, control</summary>
Setting values directly on the instance fields is also fine

```gdscript
func func_base(count: int) -> int:
    var time_before: int = Time.get_ticks_msec()
    var sum := 0
    for i in count:
        sum += 1
    finished.emit.call_deferred(Time.get_ticks_msec() - time_before)
    return sum
```

```gdscript
func func_type_check(count: int) -> int:
    var time_before: int = Time.get_ticks_msec()
    var sum := 0
    var arr: Array = [] as Array[Node]
    for i in count:
        if arr is Array[Node2D]:
            sum += 1
    finished.emit.call_deferred(Time.get_ticks_msec() - time_before)
    return sum
```

<summary>func_utility</summary>

```gdscript
func func_utility(count: int) -> int:
    var time_before: int = Time.get_ticks_msec()
    var sum := 0
    var a: Variant = 1.0
    var b: Variant = 2
    for i in count:
        sum += max(a, b)
    finished.emit.call_deferred(Time.get_ticks_msec() - time_before)
    return sum
```
